extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners working on patent classification, natural language processing, and explainable AI
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating deep-learning based patent classification systems that also produce human-understandable explanations (word-level) for their predictions using layer-wise relevance propagation (LRP). Covers model representation, training, evaluation, and visualization of explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide human-understandable explanations for predictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The system should provide human-understandable explanations for predictions (i.e., make DNN decisions less opaque and more transparent to patent experts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanations should highlight the reasons and priorities behind each prediction to build trust and promote transparency; in text-based uni-modal patent classification this is achieved by highlighting relevant words and their relevance to the prediction so users can see why the model chose a class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use layer-wise relevance propagation (LRP) to compute term relevances
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt LRP: apply the layer-wise conservation principle to calculate relevance scores by redistributing the prediction score backwards through the network layers to the input features (words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute relevance messages Ri←j according to the described redistribution rule and propagate relevance from the output neuron for class c down to input tokens. Follow established LRP procedures for recurrent and convolutional networks (references and implementation notes given).

rubrics_metrics.name: LRP numeric settings and properties (stabilizer ε and δ)
rubrics_metrics.description: LRP redistribution uses a stabilizer ε (small positive real number) and a δ parameter (0 or 1) in the relevance-message formula; the authors use ε = 0.001 and δ = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified formula for Ri←j (including the ε·sign(zj) and δ·bj terms) to avoid numerical instability. Ensure relevance conservation across layers (Ri = sum_i Ri←j) and follow the cited LRP implementations for LSTM/CNN variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance scores per input term lie in [0,1] and are interpretable by magnitude
rubrics_metrics.description: The relevance score for each relevant term is a scalar in [0,1]; higher scores represent higher relevance toward the predicted class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret and present relevance magnitudes to users (e.g., normalize or threshold as needed); use higher-intensity visual cues to indicate higher relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualize explanations by highlighting relevant words with intensity proportional to relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanations should be presented by highlighting words in the patent text, where color intensity corresponds to the computed relevance score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example visualizations highlight chemistry-related terms (alkali, alkyl, monomer, acid, acrylate) or electricity-related terms (power, channel, modem). Use color intensity to communicate contribution strength; note that some commonly-used words may also appear relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent patent text with semantic word embeddings that handle OOV/patent jargon (FastText recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent preprocessed patent text by high-dimensional distributed semantic vectors; choose embeddings that can handle out-of-vocabulary (OOV) terms common in patents (authors use FastText).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FastText (character n-gram-based) is preferred over GloVe/Word2Vec because patents contain rare or invented terms; sequence the embeddings and feed into the DNN. The paper also recommends future work to train local/patent-specific embeddings for improved domain representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train and evaluate multiple DNN architectures (Bi-LSTM, CNN, CNN-BiLSTM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Train DNN models including Bi-LSTM, CNN, and CNN-BiLSTM on the semantic representations to perform patent classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example Bi-LSTM architecture: embedding layer → Bi-LSTM(64) → Bi-LSTM(32) → FC(64, ReLU) → FC(9, softmax). Example CNN: embedding → 1D convolution → global average pooling → FC(9, softmax). Implementations used: scikit-learn and Keras. Compare architectures and select best-performing model empirically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate performance with precision, recall, and F1-score (overall and class-wise)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standard classification metrics — Precision, Recall, and F1-Score — to measure classifier performance; report both aggregate and class-wise results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present per-class metrics (example table for nine classes) and overall scores on multiple datasets. Compare metrics against related works to contextualize effectiveness; report which model performs best on each dataset (authors found Bi-LSTM led on both datasets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sufficiently large and appropriate datasets with clear train/validation/test splits
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiment on large-scale patent datasets (examples: AI-Growth-Lab dataset of 1.5M claims annotated with classes; BigPatent with ~35k labelled texts and pre-split training/validation/testing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about dataset preprocessing (claims vs human-generated abstracts), splits (BigPatent example: 25k train, 5k val, 5k test), and how dataset characteristics (e.g., abstracts vs claims) affect semantic representation and performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for class imbalance and hierarchical label structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent classification datasets are often highly imbalanced across classes and are hierarchical/multi-level (IPC has thousands of subgroups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize imbalance as an additional challenge; report class distributions (visualize where helpful) and consider methods or evaluation practices that accommodate imbalance. Note the complexity of multi-level/subgroup explanations and the need for approaches that scale to many classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support multi-label and multi-level explainability (requirement/goal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explainability should extend beyond single-label top-level classes to multi-label and hierarchical (subgroup) classification settings common in patent taxonomies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors note explaining subgroup-level predictions is more challenging and is a future direction; implementations should plan for producing explanations per predicted label in multi-label outputs and for different hierarchical levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct human-centered evaluation of generated explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Generated explanations must be evaluated with human experts (patent industry specialists) to validate usefulness and interpretability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan user-centric studies to elicit human-centric requirements and measure how explanations help experts assess predictions. Acknowledge that algorithmic plausibility (highlighted chemistry terms) does not replace formal human evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare to baseline and prior works employing similar embeddings and architectures
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate gains by comparing the proposed models and explainability approach to prior patent-classification works (e.g., models by Roudsari et al., Shaobo et al.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include direct metric comparisons (precision/recall/f1) on the same datasets and embedding choices to demonstrate consistent improvements or parity; report which metrics improve and where models fall short.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge and communicate limitations of explanations (irrelevant but informative words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept that explanations may highlight words that are not strictly field-specific but may still be useful (e.g., generic words like 'device').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document such cases and consider them during human evaluation; use domain-specific embeddings or additional preprocessing to reduce spurious relevances. Declare limitations explicitly in reporting and discussion.
